messages.text:
Could you approve a written exception to the copying and disclosure restrictions for this review? We propose the following terms.

- Four festival programmers and one outside accessibility reviewer may view the unfinished cut under confidentiality obligations. We’ll limit access to those five people and use individual streaming links wherever possible.
- Two of the five may each keep one offline screener on encrypted equipment. We’ll delete those copies and revoke viewing access when the review ends. The platform retains a backup for 30 days. Please authorize that retention, with the backup unavailable for routine viewing and deleted when the retention period expires.
- A programmer may give the selection board a short oral synopsis in a closed, confidential meeting. The board would receive no screener, stills, or clips.
- If selected, we may draft the catalog entry internally and share it with you for factual review. We propose that the written exception permit publication of the text from the festival’s official selection announcement onward, even if the film’s public release comes later. Stills, clips, and quotations from the film would require separate permission.

If you need approval over the synopsis or final catalog wording, could we agree on a short synopsis in advance and have you approve the catalog text before announcement? That would let the board deliberate and the editorial team prepare on schedule.

Speaking for the producer:

We can approve the written exception, subject to these terms.

**Review access.** Five named individuals is acceptable, provided you send us the names and roles before links are issued. Streaming links with individual watermarks are fine. Please extend the same confidentiality obligations to the accessibility reviewer as to the programmers.

**Offline screeners.** Two encrypted offline copies may be kept, but we need: (a) individualized watermarks on both, (b) written confirmation of deletion, with a deletion record copied to us, when the review ends or access is revoked, and (c) the platform backup you describe — we'll accept 30-day retention provided it is inaccessible for viewing and securely deleted at expiry, with confirmation to us.

**Oral synopsis.** Agreed — closed, confidential board meeting, no screener, stills, or clips to the board. Please keep the synopsis factual and avoid describing the final act in detail or the ending; we also ask that the cast list shared with the board not include the cameo.

**Catalog text.** We can commit to clearing draft copy within two business days of receipt. Publication may run from the festival's official selection announcement, on the conditions above about the ending and cameo — the catalog text should not reveal either. Stills, clips, and quotations require separate written permission, as you propose.

**Withdrawal and backups.** We reserve the right to withdraw the cut or revoke access at any time before announcement; on notice, all links are revoked and offline copies deleted per the procedure above. One point to resolve: if we withdraw the film after selection but before the announcement, does the catalog permission lapse automatically in your view, or should the written exception state that explicitly?

**Embargo trigger.** We're comfortable with the selection announcement as the embargo trigger for the approved synopsis only — not stills, clips, or other material. If you need the synopsis in advance for the board's deliberation, send us the short text and we'll clear it on the same two-business-day timeline.

Send the reviewer names and the draft synopsis when ready, and the proposed wording of the deletion-record obligation for the screeners, and we can close this out.

We accept the producer’s terms. We suggest making the effect of withdrawal explicit so the catalog team knows when to stop work. We propose the following wording for the written exception.

**Withdrawal and publicity.** If the producer withdraws the film before the festival’s official selection announcement, permission to draft or publish the catalog entry ends on notice, including for text already cleared. The festival will remove the entry from its publication schedule. If the producer revokes access to the cut, the festival will end viewing access immediately. A notice that only revokes viewing access leaves the film’s selection status unchanged.

**Deletion record.** At the end of review or on notice of revocation or withdrawal, whichever comes first, the festival will immediately revoke all links and require each offline viewer to delete their individually watermarked copy from their encrypted equipment. Each viewer will confirm deletion in writing, identifying the copy and the date of deletion. The festival will send the producer a copy of both records. The platform backup may remain for up to 30 days after removal of the active screener. It must be inaccessible for viewing throughout that period. The festival will verify the platform can securely delete the backup at expiry and confirm deletion before uploading the cut, then forward the deletion confirmation to the producer when issued.

**Board and catalog clearance.** We’ll submit a short factual synopsis for written clearance on the agreed two-business-day timeline. Once cleared, a programmer may deliver it orally in a closed, confidential board meeting. We’ll omit the ending and detailed discussion of the final act, exclude the cameo from any cast list, and keep the screener, stills, and clips out of the meeting. If selected, our editorial team may draft the catalog synopsis in confidence and submit it for the same two-business-day clearance. Only the approved catalog synopsis may be published, beginning with the official selection announcement and subject to the same limits on the final act, ending, and cameo. Stills, clips, and quotations require separate written permission.

Please confirm the withdrawal and deletion wording. Before links are issued, we’ll send the names and roles of the four programmers and outside accessibility reviewer and identify the two offline viewers. All five will be bound by the same confidentiality obligations, and each streaming link will carry an individual watermark. The roster and board synopsis are still to follow.

Speaking for the producer:

We confirm the withdrawal and deletion wording as drafted. Two points to make the record precise:

**Withdrawal.** Your proposed wording works — withdrawal before the selection announcement ends the catalog permission on notice, including previously cleared text, and the festival pulls the entry from its schedule. We read your last sentence as intended: a notice that revokes only viewing access does not affect selection status or the catalog permission. If that matches your understanding, we're aligned.

**Deletion record.** Agreed, including the immediate revocation, written viewer confirmations identifying the copy and deletion date, copies of both records to us, the 30-day platform backup kept inaccessible and securely deleted at expiry, and the deletion confirmation forwarded to us. One clarification on your wording: you state the festival will verify secure deletion capability "before uploading the cut" — we take that as a pre-upload verification of the platform's deletion capability, not a pre-condition on the review itself. Confirm that reading and we're aligned.

**Board and catalog clearance.** Confirmed as drafted: two-business-day clearance applies to both the board synopsis and catalog text; the ending, detailed final act, and cameo remain off-limits in both; stills, clips, and quotations need separate written permission.

Remaining open items on your side: the roster of the four programmers and accessibility reviewer, identification of the two offline viewers, and the short board synopsis. We'll turn each around within two business days of receipt.

With those delivered and cleared, the written exception is complete and we consider this workflow agreed.

We confirm both readings. Revoking viewing access alone leaves selection status and catalog permission in place. Withdrawing the film before the official selection announcement ends catalog permission on notice, even for cleared text, and we’ll pull the entry from the publication schedule.

We’ll verify the platform’s secure deletion capability before uploading the cut. That check applies to the upload and creates no separate condition for review.

The workflow terms are agreed. To complete the written exception, we still need to send you the five names and roles, identify the two offline viewers, and submit the short board synopsis for your clearance. We’ll allow two business days from receipt for clearance and will issue links only after the roster is cleared.

Speaking for the producer:

Two refinements to complete the sign-off, reflecting our final compliance arrangements.

**Watermark and access log.** For the two offline screeners, the individual watermark will be embedded in the soundtrack. We ask that the written exception reflect that, and that the festival maintain an access log for those copies — each viewing or opening session recorded by user and timestamp — with the log provided to us alongside the deletion records.

**Witnessed deletion.** We're upgrading the deletion standard: the two offline viewers will delete their copies in the presence of a witness designated by the festival (a compliance or security officer), and the written deletion confirmation will identify the watermarked copy, date, and witness. A signed witness line should accompany the viewer confirmation. The same record goes to us within a reasonable period — we'd propose five business days from deletion.

**Alternate approval.** For catalog copy and synopsis clearance, our two-business-day commitment holds, but if we're unavailable, a named alternate on our side can approve copy in my place. All other limits — no spoilers on ending, final act, or cameo; stills, clips, and quotations by separate written permission — are unchanged. The alternate has the same authority to withdraw the cut or revoke access on the producer's behalf.

Confirm these three points — soundtrack watermark with access log, witnessed deletion with signed confirmation, and acceptance of a named alternate approver — and we can close the written exception. We'll supply the alternate's name alongside the roster clearances once your five names and board synopsis arrive.

We accept the soundtrack watermark for the other offline viewer. The accessibility reviewer’s offline screen reader is incompatible with that watermark. Would you authorize one copy without the soundtrack watermark, confined to the protected screening room and accessible only through the reviewer’s separate login? It would count as one of the two offline copies. If you need an individual watermark on that copy, we can test a visual watermark with the screen reader and use it if compatible.

For both copies, we’ll log each opening or viewing session by user and timestamp. Each viewer will delete their copy when review ends or access is revoked, whichever comes first, in the presence of a festival-designated compliance or security officer. The viewer and witness will sign a record identifying the copy, deletion date, and witness. For the accessibility copy, we propose using a unique copy ID in that record. We’ll send you both the relevant access log and the signed record within five business days of each deletion. The agreed backup and withdrawal terms still apply.

We accept a named alternate with authority to clear either text, withdraw the cut, or revoke access. Press copy is due one business day before the ordinary clearance window closes. If the film is selected, may we send the proposed catalog synopsis to you and the alternate together, with the press deadline stated, and rely on either person’s written approval within one business day? We would use only the approved wording for press copy, subject to the agreed content limits and announcement embargo. If clearance misses the deadline, we’ll hold the copy. The ordinary two-business-day window works for the board synopsis.

Please confirm the accessibility arrangement and the expedited clearance path, including use of the approved synopsis for press copy at announcement. We still owe you the five names and roles, the two offline viewer designations, and the board synopsis.

Speaking for the producer:

**Accessibility copy.** We authorize one copy without the soundtrack watermark, confined to the protected screening room and accessible only through the reviewer's separate login, counting as one of the two offline copies. Our preference is that you test the visual watermark with the screen reader and use it if compatible — please report the test result with the roster. If it's incompatible, the unwatermarked copy proceeds on the terms you describe: screening-room confinement, single-login access, and a unique copy ID carried through the access log and the signed deletion record.

**Deletion and logging.** Agreed for both copies: session-level access logs by user and timestamp, deletion in the presence of a festival compliance or security officer, a signed record identifying the copy, date, and witness (copy ID in place of watermark for the accessibility copy), and delivery of the access log and signed record to us within five business days of each deletion. The backup and withdrawal terms carry over as agreed.

**Expedited clearance.** Confirmed. You may send the proposed catalog synopsis to me and the named alternate together, with the press deadline stated; either of our written approvals within one business day binds, and only approved wording goes to press, subject to the content limits and the announcement embargo. If clearance misses the deadline, you hold the copy — we'd add one clarification: if the deadline passes without a response from either of us, that's a hold, not a deemed approval. Confirm that reading and we're aligned.

We'll rely on the alternate only for clearance, withdrawal, and revocation as you state — press approval beyond the catalog synopsis still runs through the ordinary separate-permission route for stills, clips, and quotations.

Still outstanding from you: the five names and roles, the two offline viewer designations, the watermark test result for the accessibility copy, and the board synopsis. We'll respond within the agreed windows.

Confirmed. If the press deadline passes without written approval from you or the named alternate, we’ll hold the copy. Silence never authorizes release. A later written clearance allows us to use the approved catalog synopsis at or after the official selection announcement. Stills, clips, and quotations each require separate written permission.

We’ll test the visual watermark and use it if compatible. If it interferes with the screen reader, we’ll use the authorized unwatermarked copy in the protected screening room under the reviewer’s separate login, with its unique ID in the access log and signed deletion record.

The workflow terms are agreed. We still owe you the five names and roles, the two offline viewer designations, the watermark test result, and the short board synopsis for clearance.

Speaking for the producer:

We confirm the fallback plan: if the visual watermark interferes with the screen reader, the unwatermarked authorized copy may be used in the protected screening room under the reviewer's separate login, with its unique ID in the access log and a signed deletion record. We treat that record under the same deletion-record obligations already agreed.

We also confirm: silence never authorizes release, the press deadline copy is held absent written approval from us or the named alternate, and a later written clearance permits use of the approved catalog synopsis from the official selection announcement. Stills, clips, and quotations remain subject to separate written permission.

All workflow terms are agreed. We await the roster, offline viewer designations, watermark test result, and board synopsis, and will clear each within two business days of receipt.
